text: dsh-pptx-builder 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 PowerPoint 制作插件，通过注册的工具创建、扩展和检查演示文稿。它提供多种幻灯片模板，可添加格式化文本、图片、图表、代码卡片和 LaTeX 公式，并支持更新或移除页面元素。适合希望在 DSH 会话中生成可编辑 PPTX 的用户。使用图表、代码卡片和公式渲染需可用的 Python/Pillow 环境；插入网络图片时会下载图片并嵌入文稿。

dsh-pptx-builder adds PowerPoint tools to DeepSeek Harness. Create and edit decks with slide templates, text, images, charts, code cards, and LaTeX formulas; inspect or revise slide elements. Python with Pillow is needed for chart, code, and formula rendering. URL images are downloaded and embedded.
想在 DSH 里直接生成可以继续编辑的 PowerPoint。
帮我用模板排版幻灯片，再加图表、代码片段和公式。
I want to inspect and revise elements in an existing PPTX deck from my DSH session.
dsh-pptx-builder 的「创建幻灯片」功能：创建 PPTX 后，可按标题、内容、分栏、图表或公式等模板追加页面。通过 pptx_create 和 pptx_add_slide 工具设置布局与文本。
dsh-pptx-builder 的「添加视觉内容」功能：可向幻灯片添加图片、图表、代码卡片或 LaTeX 公式；图表、代码及公式会渲染成图片后嵌入。通过相应 pptx_add_* 工具传入内容和文件路径。
dsh-pptx-builder 使用前须知：通过图片 URL 添加图片时，插件会向该 URL 发起 HTTP(S) 请求并将返回的图片嵌入演示文稿。

dsh-pptx-builder README · PowerPoint Builder for DeepSeek Harness：A plugin bundle that lets an agent build real Microsoft PowerPoint decks: pastel
palettes, ten reusable slide templates with exact geometric centering, styled
text boxes, internet images, charts rendered by Python, highlighted code cards,
and LaTeX formulas — matrices, integrals, sums with limits — typeset by the
plugin itself, with no LaTeX installation. It also ships a **Presentations**
agent mode tuned for deck work.

dsh-pptx-builder README · PowerPoint Builder for DeepSeek Harness：The `.pptx` package (ZIP + OOXML) is written by the plugin itself, so there is
no Office dependency, no network round-trip after an image is embedded, and the
file stays valid after every call.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Install：Install the bundle into the current profile:

```text
plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "dsh-pptx-builder" }
```

Or use **Plugins → Install** in the Harness UI and paste the package name.
After a restart the tools show up in every mode, and a new **Presentations**
agent preset appears in the mode picker for a new session.

From a local checkout, pass the absolute directory instead of the package name.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Presentations mode：The preset adds a persona that knows the workflow — inspect before editing,
build from templates, cite data sources, typeset mathematics with
`pptx_add_math`, finish with `present` — plus a focused toolset: the `pptx_*`
tools, file reading, web search/fetch, `present`, `todo_write`,
`ask_user_question`, and compaction. The tools themselves are registered
host-wide, so they are also usable outside this mode.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pptx_create` | Creates a deck on a pastel palette: size (`16:9` / `4:3`), palette, default font, accent, page-number placement. |
| `pptx_gallery` | Builds a ready-made reference deck: `features` tours every template, alignment, list style and chart kind; `showcase` is a polished business deck. |
| `pptx_add_slide` | Adds a slide from a template (`title`, `section`, `content`, `split-left`, `split-right`, `chart`, `code`, `closing`, `blank`) with a heading, text, presenter and photo. |
| `pptx_add_text` | Arbitrary text box: `role`, `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`, `font_size`/`font_face`/`bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`color`/`align`/`valign`/`bullet`. |
| `pptx_add_image` | Downloads an image by `url` (or reads a local `path`), embeds the bytes and places it; the aspect ratio is preserved. |
| `pptx_add_chart` | Renders a chart from data (bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie, donut) with Python and embeds it. |
| `pptx_add_code` | Renders a code snippet as a dark card with syntax highlighting, line numbers, a file-name header and highlighted lines. |
| `pptx_add_math` | Typesets a LaTeX formula — matrices, integrals, sums with li

dsh-pptx-builder README · Tools：Coordinates are inches from the top-left corner of the slide (16:9 is
13.333 × 7.5), font sizes are points, colours are `#RRGGBB`, a basic colour
name, or a palette keyword (`ink`, `muted`, `accent`, `background`).

dsh-pptx-builder README · Templates：| Template | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Oversized centred heading, subtitle below, presenter line in the bottom-right corner. Page number off. |
| `section` | Divider: heading and subtitle centred on the slide. |
| `content` | Centred heading on top, a fixed-width text column underneath. |
| `split-right` | Photo fitted and centred in the right half; heading and text centred in the left half. |
| `split-left` | Mirrored: photo on the left, text on the right. |
| `chart` | Heading and caption on top, the lower two thirds reserved for `pptx_add_chart`. |
| `code` | Heading and subtitle on top, the rest reserved for `pptx_add_code`. |
| `math` | Heading and subtitle on top, an optional statement under them, the rest reserved for `pptx_add_math`. |
| `closing` | Large centred "Спасибо за внимание" (override with `title`), optional subtitle. |
| `blank` | Nothing but the background. |

dsh-pptx-builder README · Templates：Every template centres its content inside its own region: the photo in its half,
the heading and text in theirs, blocks centered vertically.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Palettes：`pptx_create` takes `palette`: `sand` (default), `mint`, `lavender`, `sky`,
`rose`. A palette defines the pastel background of every slide, the body ink,
the muted secondary colour, the accent, and the chart series colours.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Alignment and lists：Alignment and text shape are parameters, not template defaults:

| Parameter | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `align` | `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify` for the `text` block |
| `title_align` | the same for the heading and subtitle |
| `bullet` | `true` for a bulleted list, `false` (default) for one solid block |

dsh-pptx-builder README · Alignment and lists：Defaults: `content` is left-aligned, `split-left` / `split-right` are centred
without bullets and left-aligned with them. Long lists read best on the left;
centred or right-aligned text suits short lines and single paragraphs. An
existing block can be re-aligned with `pptx_update_element` (`align`, `bullet`).

dsh-pptx-builder README · Charts：`pptx_add_chart` accepts data, not code:

```json
{ "file": "sales.pptx", "kind": "bar", "stacked": false,
  "categories": ["2021", "2022", "2023", "2024"],
  "series": [ { "name": "Revenue", "values": [10.2, 13.8, 17.1, 21.4] } ],
  "y_label": "bn RUB", "value_format": "auto",

dsh-pptx-builder README · Charts：Supported: `bar` (including `stacked`), `line`, `area`, `pie`, `donut`. The
renderer draws the palette background, a light grid, axis labels, a legend,
value labels and a source footnote. The image is 1800 × 1000 px and is embedded
into the deck.

Data pipeline: `web_search` / `web_fetch` find the numbers, the model puts them
into `categories` and `series`, `pptx_add_chart` draws the picture, and
`pptx_update_element` can move or resize it.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Code cards：`pptx_add_code` renders a snippet into a dark rounded card — syntax
highlighting, line numbers, a file-name header, a language chip, and an accent
band on highlighted lines — and embeds it as a picture.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Code cards：Languages: `python`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `bash`, `sql`, `text`.
Keep lines under ~90 characters and the snippet under 60 lines: the card scales
as a whole, so one long line shrinks all the code. The card is a picture — to
change the code, remove the element and add it again.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Formulas：`pptx_add_math` typesets LaTeX into a transparent 300 dpi PNG and embeds it.
The formula is laid out by the plugin's own typesetter (`python/math.py`), so a
machine without TeX produces the same result, and the picture is placed at its
natural typographic size: a 44 pt formula is 44 pt tall on the slide.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Formulas：| Construct | Syntax |
| --- | --- |
| Fractions, binomials | `\frac{a}{b}`, `\dfrac`, `\tfrac`, `\binom{n}{k}` |
| Roots | `\sqrt{x}`, `\sqrt[3]{x}` |
| Scripts | `x_i^2`, `\sum_{k=1}^{n}`, `\int_0^1`, `\lim_{x \to 0}` |
| Big operators | `\sum \prod \coprod \int \iint \iiint \oint \bigcup \bigcap \bigoplus` |
| Matrices | `matrix`, `pmatrix`, `bmatrix`, `Bmatrix`, `vmatrix`, `Vmatrix` |
| Systems, derivations | `cases`, `aligned` (`&` aligns, `\\` breaks a line), `array{cc}` |
| Delimiters | `\left( ... \right)`, `\left[ ... \right]`, `\left\{ ... \right.`, `\langle \rangle`, `\|x\|` |
| Greek | `\alpha` … `\omega`, `\Gamma` … `\Omega`, `\varepsilon`, `\varphi`, `\vartheta` |
| Letter styles | `\mathbb{R}`, `\mathcal{L}`, `\mathbf{v}`, `\boldsymbol{\alpha}`, `\mathrm{d}`, `\operatorname{rank}` |
| Accents | `\vec{a}`, `\hat{x}`, `\bar{x}`, `\tilde{x}`, `\dot{x}`, `\ddot{x}`, `\overline{AB}` |
| Symbols | `\partial \nabla \infty \pm \cdot \times \le \ge \ne \approx \equiv \in \notin \subset \subseteq \to \Rightarrow \Leftrightarrow \forall \exists` |
| Words | `\text{если } x > 0` |

dsh-pptx-builder README · Formulas：The `math` template leaves the lower part of the slide free; `pptx_add_math`
places the formula there, centred, and shrinks it only if it would not fit.
`font_size` 40–56 pt suits a key result, 28–32 pt a secondary line. A
multi-line derivation stays in one call:

```json
{ "latex": "\\begin{aligned} (a+b)^2 &= a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \\\\ &= a^2 + b^2 + 2ab \\end{aligned}" }
```

dsh-pptx-builder README · Formulas：An unsupported command fails with its position instead of producing a wrong
slide: `unsupported command \fraq at position 1`. Delimiters a model tends to
add (`$...$`, `\[...\]`, `\begin{equation}`) are stripped automatically.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Examples：`pptx_gallery` builds reference decks from code, so they always match the
current templates:

| `style` | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `features` | A tour: all ten templates, three alignments, list and solid text, both split slides, four chart kinds, two code cards, four formula slides, palettes and settings. |
| `showcase` | A polished ten-slide business deck: title, context, charts, photo slides, a metrics code card, closing. |

dsh-pptx-builder README · Deck state：A `.pptx` cannot be edited incrementally without a model, so the plugin keeps
the deck document in `<name>.pptx.json` beside the presentation and rebuilds the
package from it on every change. The sidecar is the editable source; the `.pptx`
is always a valid output. Deleting the sidecar does not break the presentation,
but makes it not editable by the plugin.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Configuration：Optional `config` fields on the `pptx-builder` Loader row:

| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font` | `Calibri` | Default text font. |
| `accent` | from the palette | Accent colour overriding the palette. |
| `maxImageBytes` | `20971520` | Size limit for a downloaded image (20 MB). |
| `pythonPath` | auto-detected | Python interpreter with Pillow for charts and code cards. |

dsh-pptx-builder README · Requirements：- Charts and code cards are rendered by Python with Pillow. Harness ships such
  a runtime, and the plugin finds it automatically; on another setup point
  `pythonPath` at an interpreter where `import PIL` works.
- Images must be direct PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP links. WebP and SVG are rejected
  with an actionable message, because PowerPoint cannot render them.

dsh-pptx-builder README · Limitations：- Charts cover bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie and donut. No maps, heatmaps or
  3D charts.
- Formulas are high-resolution pictures, not editable PowerPoint equations: to
  change one, remove the element and add it again. The typesetter covers the
  subset above, not the whole LaTeX language — no equation numbering, `\tikz`,
  chemistry packages or custom macros.
- Photo templates fit the whole image (contain); there is no cropping.
- Animations, speaker notes, tables and native PowerPoint charts are not
  created.
- An image is downloaded when the tool runs; after that the deck is
  self-contained.
